subject: api/src/lib/redis.ts:163 — «DB منبعِ حقیقتِ ضدِ double-booking است»
verdict_summary: With the reservation slot lock fully failed open (Redis unreachable), the database alone still guarantees exactly one winner per physical table+slot. Proven live and concurrently on a real Postgres. Correctness is preserved by TWO mechanisms: the no_table_overlap EXCLUDE constraint (primary table_id) and the SERIALIZABLE isolation level plus in-transaction re-check (merged secondary tables, which EXCLUDE is structurally blind to). Before this pass the second mechanism had zero test coverage: deleting it left all 11 pre-existing concurrency tests green with exit 0.

environment.scratch_db: rezervno_slotlock on rezv-test-pg:55432 (created for this pass; rezervno_a11 untouched)
environment.dev_db: rezervno on rezervno-postgres — read-only queries only, not modified
environment.note: RLS is inert here (61 tables enabled, 0 policies, owner+SUPERUSER+BYPASSRLS) and is not cited as a control anywhere in this report.

findings.claim: The parenthetical at api/src/lib/redis.ts:163 is TRUE: with the slot lock failed open, the database alone prevents double-booking. A Redis outage costs throughput, error-message quality and latency — not correctness.
findings.evidence: Deterministic write-skew, two concurrent psql sessions, both reading before either writes, on the live scratch DB. SERIALIZABLE: 'ERROR: could not serialize access due to read/write dependencies among transactions / DETAIL: Reason code: Canceled on identification as a pivot, during write.' → 1 row committed, physical-overlap detector returned 0 rows, T1_PSQL_EXIT=0 T2_PSQL_EXIT=0 GROUNDTRUTH_EXIT=0 SCRIPT_EXIT=0. Application level: 10 concurrent createReservation calls through the REAL withSlotLock fail-open branch → {"ok":1,"codes":{"TABLE_CONFLICT":9},"db_active_rows":1,"physical_overlaps":0}; control arm with a working Redis lock identical.
findings.verified_by: api/tests/slot-lock-failopen-double-booking.test.mts (7 tests, exit 0) + scratchpad interleave scripts; constraint confirmed in api/prisma/sql/026-consolidate-exclusion-constraint.sql:70-79, absent-by-necessity from api/prisma/schema.prisma (grep count 0), and byte-identical on BOTH live databases.

findings.claim: Half of that safety property was completely unguarded. Downgrading reservations.ts:396 from Serializable to ReadCommitted keeps the entire pre-existing concurrency and lock suite green — including the describe named 'C2 — قفلِ Redis کاملاً fail-open — DB به‌تنهایی هنوز محافظت می‌کند'. That is a gate that passes with the feature deleted.
findings.evidence: Mutation M3 at api/src/lib/reservations.ts:396. tests/redis.test.mts + tests/table-merge-occupancy-concurrency.test.mts → 'ℹ tests 11 / ℹ pass 11 / ℹ fail 0', EXISTING_EXIT=0. Under the same mutation the new gate fails with 'هیچ SIReadLockی روی reservations دیده نشد ⇒ تراکنشِ درجِ رزرو SERIALIZABLE نیست' AND with a genuine product-path double-booking: 'دقیقاً یک برنده انتظار می‌رود، 2 تا شد' — ONEFILE_EXIT=1. Reverted with git checkout; reservations.ts:396 confirmed back to Serializable.

findings.claim: createWalkin can seat a guest on a table that is already physically occupied as the SECONDARY table of an active merged reservation. No concurrency, no Redis outage, no attacker — a plain sequential staff action on the happy path. createWalkin never calls getOccupiedTableNumbers, and createWalkinTx runs at default (READ COMMITTED) isolation, so its only guard is the EXCLUDE constraint, which keys on table_id and cannot see merged secondaries.
findings.evidence: Live sequential probe on the scratch DB with a positive control. Control (walk-in aimed at the PRIMARY table of the active merge): {"step":"control-primary-841","outcome":"REJECTED code=TABLE_CONFLICT"} — the constraint does fire, so the probe is valid. Actual: {"step":"walkin-on-merged-SECONDARY-842","outcome":"ACCEPTED code=RZJGXRVX2 table=842"} then {"step":"ground-truth","physical_overlaps":1,"detail":[{"num":842}]} and rows [{"code":"RZJGXRVX2","num":842,"merged":[]},{"code":"WKM-845f","num":841,"merged":[841,842]}]. WALKIN_PROBE_EXIT=0.
findings.verified_by: scratch probe api/tests/_probe-walkin-merged.mts (removed after the run; reproduction steps in decision_package.reproduction below). Code: api/src/lib/reservations.ts createWalkin/createWalkinTx; blindness documented by the repo itself at api/src/lib/table-occupancy.ts:5-19.

findings.claim: The build machine is at 100% disk usage with zero bytes free. At that point the agent harness itself cannot write, and Postgres queries against the scratch DB time out. Any test result produced on this machine while it is in that state must be treated as suspect until re-run with headroom.
findings.evidence: df -h /c → 'C: 119G 119G 0 100% /c'. Harness failure: "ENOSPC: no space left on device, open '.../tasks/b4b7zroq9.output'". A plain `docker exec ... psql -c "SELECT count(*) ..."` exceeded a 120s timeout. The abandoned probe's real termination cause was "tee: 'standard output': No space left on device / [exited with code 1]", and it never printed its own PROBE_EXIT marker (grep -c PROBE_EXIT → 0).
findings.verified_by: raw df output and harness error above; ~110MB freed from my own and stale temp task outputs solely to be able to write this record. The 119GB was NOT reclaimed — deciding what to delete (docker images/volumes, node_modules, .next caches) is an ops decision and was escalated rather than taken.

findings.claim: I attributed the mid-investigation probe stall to a cross-transaction gate in my Prisma interleave that never resolves when one side aborts. That was a hypothesis stated as a finding. The raw evidence shows the process died on ENOSPC / a blocked stdout pipe. The gate-deadlock explanation is WITHDRAWN.
findings.evidence: Abandoned task output: "tee: 'standard output': No space left on device" then "[exited with code 1]"; no PROBE_EXIT marker was ever printed. Corrected in audit/round-20/SLOT-LOCK-FAILOPEN.md §11 and in two source comments in api/tests/slot-lock-failopen-double-booking.test.mts (the gateless interleave design is kept on its own merits, not because the hypothesis was confirmed).
findings.verified_by: no conclusion in this report depends on that claim — the §4a interleave evidence comes from psql sessions, not from that probe. Residual uncertainty explicitly recorded: 'the fix is why layer 2 is green' is not fully separable from 'the disk freed up'; a re-run on a machine with headroom is the outstanding verification.

findings.claim: Three defects in my own work, reported before anyone found them: (a) probe v1 spaced scenarios 60 min apart while a booking blocks for 105 min, producing 7 false 'failures'; (b) the first control interleave passed a quoted isolation level so BEGIN was a syntax error and the sessions ran in autocommit rather than explicit transactions; (c) the first version of layer 2 used a fixed 2.5s observation window that passed standalone and failed inside the full 1542-test run, and its blocked-session detector filtered on pg_locks.database, which is NULL for transactionid locks — the exact lock type an EXCLUDE wait takes.
findings.evidence: (a) scratchpad probe-2.log, 7 FAIL lines all of form 'got 0' where 0 winners was the correct answer; fixed by one restaurant per scenario. (b) 'psql:<stdin>:3: ERROR: syntax error at or near ''read committed''' — re-run correctly, same conclusion. (c) full-test.log line 4009 vs three consecutive green standalone runs; after switching to pg_stat_activity (datname=current_database() AND wait_event_type='Lock') the test passes 3/3 and runs in ~580ms instead of ~2600ms.
findings.verified_by: all three corrections re-verified; no assertion was weakened — (a) and (c) were mechanism fixes, and the (a)/(c) assertions became strictly harder to satisfy.

decision_package.title: createWalkin can double-book a merged secondary table
decision_package.requires: architect sign-off — touches the reservation lifecycle. NOT implemented in this pass.
decision_package.verbatim_source: api/src/lib/reservations.ts, createWalkin: `if (input.tableId) { const t = await db.table.findUnique({ where: { id: input.tableId } }); if (!t || t.restaurantId !== input.restaurantId) throw Err.notFound('میز'); if (!t.isActive || t.state === 'maintenance') throw Err.tableUnavailable(t.number); }` — there is no occupancy check of any kind, and createWalkinTx calls `db.$transaction(async (tx) => {...})` with no isolationLevel option (default READ COMMITTED).
decision_package.reproduction: 1) restaurant with tables 841 and 842, both isMergeable, mergeableWith each other. 2) INSERT an active merged reservation: table_id = 841, merged_table_numbers = {841,842}, status 'seated', slot_start now-10min, slot_end now+80min. 3) createWalkin({ tableId: <841> }) → must be REJECTED with TABLE_CONFLICT (positive control, proves EXCLUDE fires). 4) createWalkin({ tableId: <842> }) → currently ACCEPTED. 5) run the primary+merged overlap detector → 1 row on table 842.
depends_on: api/src/lib/table-occupancy.ts:5-19 — already documents that EXCLUDE covers primary table_id only
api/src/lib/reservations.ts:373 — the equivalent check createReservation performs inside its transaction
prisma/sql/026-consolidate-exclusion-constraint.sql:70-79 — the constraint whose blind spot this is

options.option: A — add the in-transaction occupancy check to createWalkinTx and raise its isolation to Serializable
options.cost: small: one call to getOccupiedTableNumbers(tx, ...) before the insert, plus the isolationLevel option and a retry loop for 40001. Mirrors placeReservation exactly, so no new pattern.
options.blast_radius: walk-in path only. Staff will start seeing TABLE_CONFLICT where the operation silently succeeded before — which is the point, but it is a behaviour change on a path staff use under time pressure. Serializable adds retry-able 40001s that createWalkin does not currently handle.
options.reversibility: high — pure application code, revert is a git revert; no schema change, no migration.

options.option: B — model merged secondary tables as real rows (a blocker reservation per secondary table) so the EXCLUDE constraint covers them
options.cost: large: data model change, a migration, and every reader of reservations (availability, analytics, panel lists, cancellation, lifecycle) must learn to filter blocker rows.
options.blast_radius: very wide — every consumer of the reservations table. Would also make table-occupancy.ts's UNION branch redundant and close the whole class of merge blindness at once, including M5.
options.reversibility: low — a schema and data migration; reverting after production data exists is expensive.

options.option: C — accept and document the risk
options.blast_radius: a restaurant seats two parties at one physical table. Recovery is manual and happens in front of the guest.

decision_package.recommendation: Option A before launch, Option B recorded as the real structural fix for after launch. A is the same shape as the guard createReservation already has, is cheap, and is reversible; B is correct but is a data-model change and cannot be justified on this timeline. Whichever is chosen, it ships with a regression test imported in api/tests/_all.runner.mts, plus its own mutation round with recorded exit codes.
decision_package.not_done_deliberately: No fix implemented, no commit made, and no alert rule added — the alert belongs to round-20's observability scope and needs its own promtool falsifiability pass against observability/alerts.test.yml.
